title: Maximum Rows Covered by Columns
statement:
You get a grid `matrix` of 0s and 1s with `m` rows and `n` columns, and an integer `numSelect`. Choose exactly `numSelect` different columns.

A row counts as covered when every column where that row holds a 1 is one of your chosen columns. A row made only of 0s is always covered.

Return the largest number of covered rows that any choice of `numSelect` columns can reach.
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 12 columns there are at most 2^12 = 4096 column sets, so trying every set of exactly `numSelect` columns is cheap. Writing each row as a bitmask of the columns holding a 1 makes the coverage test a single operation: the row is covered when its mask has no bit outside the chosen set, that is `(mask & selected) === mask`. A row of zeros has mask 0 and passes automatically.

## Approach

1. Turn every row into `mask`, setting bit `j` when `row[j]` is 1, and store the masks in `rowMasks`.
2. Loop `selected` over every number from 0 to 2^n - 1; each one is a set of columns.
3. Count its set bits in `bits` (clearing the lowest bit each step) and skip it unless `bits` equals `numSelect`.
4. Count the rows whose mask fits inside `selected` in `covered`.
5. Keep the largest `covered` in `best` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 3`. The row masks are `0` (row 0), `0b101 = 5` (row 1), `0b110 = 6` (row 2) and `0b100 = 4` (row 3). The sets with two columns are:

- `selected = 3` (columns 0 and 1): only row 0 fits, so `covered = 1`.
- `selected = 5` (columns 0 and 2): rows 0, 1 and 3 fit, `covered = 3`.
- `selected = 6` (columns 1 and 2): rows 0, 2 and 3 fit, `covered = 3`.

So `best = 3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(2^n · (n + m)): each of the 2^n sets costs a bit count and one check per row.
- Space: O(m) for the row masks.

## Pitfalls

- Exactly `numSelect` columns must be chosen. Choosing more never hurts coverage, so allowing larger sets would overcount.
- Write the test as `(mask & selected) === mask`, with the parentheses: in JavaScript, Java and C `===`/`==` binds tighter than `&`.
- Rows of zeros are covered by every choice; do not skip them.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of columns |
| `rowMasks` | one bitmask per row: the columns holding a 1 |
| `selected` | the current set of chosen columns as a bitmask |
| `bits` | how many columns `selected` contains |
| `covered` | rows covered by `selected` |
| `best` | the most rows covered by any valid set so far |
